input.new_string:
#
# After a failure the test runner is relaunched for the rest, and xcodebuild
# can then sit for up to 600 s after the last test, waiting on the first
# runner (seen serially on 2026-09-23 and in a shard on 2026-09-25). So once
# every test of the pass has reported and the log has been quiet for 60 s,
# xcodebuild is stopped and the pass fails, saying why.
run_tests() {   # $1 = label, $2 = tests in the pass, rest = -only-testing/-skip-testing args
    local label=$1 want=$2 log="$LOG_DIR/$1.log"; shift 2
    local from=(-project Latchkey.xcodeproj -scheme Latchkey -configuration Testing
                -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData)
    [[ -n "$XCTESTRUN" ]] && from=(-xctestrun "$XCTESTRUN")
    (cd "$APP" && exec xcodebuild test-without-building "${from[@]}" \
        -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" -resultBundlePath "$LOG_DIR/$label.xcresult" \
        -parallel-testing-enabled NO -test-timeouts-enabled YES \
        -default-test-execution-time-allowance 120 "$@") > "$log" 2>&1 &
    local pid=$! size=-1 quiet=0 reported
    while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        sleep 2
        reported=$(grep -cE "^Test Case '.*' (passed|failed) \(" "$log")
        if [[ $reported -ge $want && $(stat -f %z "$log") == "$size" ]]; then
            quiet=$(( quiet + 2 ))
        else
            quiet=0; size=$(stat -f %z "$log")
        fi
        if [[ $quiet -ge 60 ]]; then
            echo "error: xcodebuild ($label) was still running 60 s after all $want tests reported;" >&2
            echo "       stopped it (after a runner relaunch it can wait 600 s for nothing)" >&2
            kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid"
            return 1
        fi
    done
    wait "$pid"
}

#
# After a failure the test runner is relaunched for the rest, and xcodebuild
# can then sit for up to 600 s after the last test, waiting on the first
# runner (seen serially on 2026-09-23 and in a shard on 2026-09-25). So once
# every test of the pass has reported and the log has been quiet for 60 s,
# xcodebuild is stopped and the pass fails, saying why.
run_tests() {   # $1 = label, $2 = tests in the pass, rest = -only-testing/-skip-testing args
    local label=$1 want=$2 log="$LOG_DIR/$1.log"; shift 2
    local from=(-project Latchkey.xcodeproj -scheme Latchkey -configuration Testing
                -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData)
    [[ -n "$XCTESTRUN" ]] && from=(-xctestrun "$XCTESTRUN")
    (cd "$APP" && exec xcodebuild test-without-building "${from[@]}" \
        -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" -resultBundlePath "$LOG_DIR/$label.xcresult" \
        -parallel-testing-enabled NO -test-timeouts-enabled YES \
        -default-test-execution-time-allowance 120 "$@") > "$log" 2>&1 &
    local pid=$! size=-1 quiet=0 reported
    while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        sleep 2
        reported=$(grep -cE "^Test Case '.*' (passed|failed) \(" "$log")
        if [[ $reported -ge $want && $(stat -f %z "$log") == "$size" ]]; then
            quiet=$(( quiet + 2 ))
        else
            quiet=0; size=$(stat -f %z "$log")
        fi
        if [[ $quiet -ge 60 ]]; then
            echo "error: xcodebuild ($label) was still running 60 s after all $want tests reported;" >&2
            echo "       stopped it (after a runner relaunch it can wait 600 s for nothing)" >&2
            kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid"
            return 1
        fi

All four files are committed and the tree is clean on `main`. Nothing was pushed, and no suite was run this turn.

**Commits:**
- `6a114a9` l1: run the offline suite across four simulators by default
- `bd1adc4` l1: name every test of a killed shard and stop xcodebuild's idle wait
- `2050323` l1: lead shard failures with file:line and drop watchdog noise
- `20aa1b6` docs: record F14 stage 2, the sharded L1 runner

**What changed in the doc since last turn:**
```diff
--- /Users/olof/src/latchkey/docs/features/F14-fast-suites.md
+++ /Users/olof/src/latchkey/docs/features/F14-fast-suites.md
@@ -497,1 +497,1 @@
-| serial, `--serial` | 38/38 | 572 s |
+| serial, `--serial`, with the final `run_tests` | 38/38 | 574 s |
@@ -501,1 +501,2 @@
-Names: the serial run and a sharded run each passed 38. Both lists `diff`
+Names: two serial runs (572 s before the watchdog's last change, 574 s
+after it) and a sharded run each passed 38. The lists `diff`
```

**The measured figures in the F14 §9 entry,** all read from the run logs:

| Run | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| N=4, warm | 38/38 | 169 s, then 168 s |
| N=4, right after a simulator re-boot (run10) | 38/38 | 189 s |
| N=2 | 38/38 | 304 s (projection was 303–309 s) |
| Serial, `--serial` (run11) | 38/38 | 574 s |
| N=4, one assertion deliberately broken | 37/38, 1 failed | 188 s |
| N=4, Shard 3 shut down mid-run (run9) | 37/38, 1 not run | 343 s |

- **Names:** I diffed run11's 38 test names against the file's `func test…` list; they match exactly, as do the earlier serial and sharded lists.
- **Induced failure:** reported under its own test name, with its assertion text, shard and simulator.
- **Dead simulator:** `testDashboardLoadsThroughTheProxy` is named as never reporting, and shard 3 fails with the watchdog's message and "simulator … is Shutdown after the run".

**Not exercised by a run:** the changes in `2050323`. They only change how failures are printed:
- Failure text now comes from the log, with file:line. I checked that on run8's shard 2 log, not in a full failing run.
- A not-run test no longer prints "(no failure message recorded)".
- A `2>/dev/null` hides bash's "Terminated: 15" notice.

I committed them because nothing in the doc claims they were run. run10 did go through the new merge line, but only with passing tests.

**Two things left open, both written in the doc:**
- The 240 s budget is unchanged; F14 §7.4 asks for it to be re-set once the figure settles.
- `/Users/olof/src/latchkey/scripts/l1-durations.txt` has to be refreshed by hand from a run's `durations.txt`.

**Simulators:** `Latchkey Shard 1–4` are still booted. `/Users/olof/src/latchkey/scripts/test-offline-shards.py sims down` shuts them down, and `sims delete` removes them.

The @kirocrew-computer, @kirocrew-core, @kirocrew-cron and @kirocrew-work MCP servers were not available; nothing here needed them. The Excalidraw, Expedia, Slack and Tripadvisor connectors need authorising in claude.ai's connector settings before they can be used.
